authority_rule: The original published study is the only source of truth. Every claim scored must trace to one of this study's primary_sources, with a page, table or figure reference. If a finding in this registry is not supported by the source, mark it not_testable with reason claim_not_in_any_source and say so; the registry can be wrong, the study cannot.

primary_sources.cite: Carroll et al., PLOS Genetics 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1002117

replication_targets.finding: S106P and L111Q switch AncCR specificity toward cortisol; introduced alone into AncCR they yield a non-functional receptor.
replication_targets.source: Ortlund 2007; residue tokens S106P and L111Q appear 11 and 10 times
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon rank the 106-111 pair as coupled, and does it place the permissive group before them in the ordering?

replication_targets.finding: Permissive substitutions (group X) include Y27R, L29M, F98I, Q105L, N26T, S212D; they are required before the switch is tolerated.
replication_targets.test: Recall of these positions among epistaeon's detected partners of 106/111.

replication_targets.finding: Reversal is blocked: from AncGR2, reversing the group X function-switching substitutions (S106P, L111Q) yields a non-functional receptor (AncGR2-x), as does AncGR2-xyz and every combination restoring group x. Reversing the restrictive substitutions first does not restore ancestral function.
replication_targets.test: MEASURED ORDER. The study establishes a direction: forward through group X is viable, reverse through group X is not. Does epistaeon infer the same directional constraint between these substitutions? Judge the inferred order only; how epistaeon arrives at it internally is not under test.

replication_targets.finding: Order constraint among forward substitutions: introducing group Y (L29M, F98I, deletion S212D) into AncGR1 or into AncGR1+X produces completely non-functional receptors. Introducing group Z (N26T, Q105L) into the non-functional AncGR1+X+Y receptor restores transcriptional activity, so Z is permissive for Y. The historically likely pathways are those in which groups Z and X occurred before group Y was complete.
replication_targets.source: Ortlund 2007, Fig. 3A and 3C; group definitions given verbatim in the text
replication_targets.test: MEASURED ORDER. The study establishes that group Z must precede group Y. Does epistaeon place Z before Y in its inferred order of substitutions? Judge the inferred order only; how epistaeon arrives at it internally is not under test.
replication_targets.scope_note: Order evidence exists only for the assayed substitutions: group X (S106P, L111Q), group Y (L29M, F98I, S212D) and group Z (N26T, Q105L). Score epistaeon's order over these substitutions. The remainder of the 37-substitution interval has no published order evidence and must not be scored.

structures.notes: 7PRX is the wild-type human GR ligand-binding domain, 2.20 A, residues 529-776 complete, numbering equal to UniProt P04150. The resurrected ancestral receptors (AncCR 2Q1H/2Q1V/2Q3Y, AncGR1 3RY9, AncGR2 3GN8) are in ../data/ancestral_coordinates/ and use local LBD numbering: add 531 to reach human GR. In 3GN8 that offset breaks after about position 212.

known_limitations: The NR3C1 TOGA2 reference is the GR-gamma isoform: positions after 451 are one higher than UniProt / 7PRX numbering. Misapplying this shifts the entire ligand-binding domain by one residue, silently.
Order evidence covers only the 7 assayed substitutions in groups X, Y and Z; the rest of the AncGR1 to AncGR2 interval (37 substitutions total) was never assayed for order.
The Carroll 2011 stability table is calculated, not measured.
No cortisol-bound ancestral structure exists. 2Q1V is titled cortisol but its deposited ligand is prednisone.
expected_outcome_note: The strongest case available, and the only one with measured mutation order. SR1 and SR2 test site identification; SR3 and SR4 test inferred order against assayed intermediates.
